title: A finite source mapping fibre-injectively into a flat target is flat
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A,\mathfrak m_B$, meaning that the inverse image of $\mathfrak m_B$ is $\mathfrak m_A$. Assume this homomorphism is essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. Let $N,M$ be $B$-modules and $u:N\to M$ a $B$-linear map. Suppose $N$ is finite over $B$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], $M$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and the induced map
$$\overline u:N/\mathfrak m_AN\longrightarrow M/\mathfrak m_AM$$
is injective. Here $\mathfrak m_AN$ and $\mathfrak m_AM$ are the submodules generated by products of images of elements of $\mathfrak m_A$ with module elements. Then $N$ is flat over $A$ and finitely presented over $B$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Moreover $u$ is $A$-universally injective: for every $A$-module $Q$, the map $u\otimes_A1_Q:N\otimes_AQ\to M\otimes_AQ$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No finite generation assumption is made on $M$, and neither $A$ nor $B$ is assumed Noetherian.

proof.text: First prove the following auxiliary implication for any henselian local $A$, local essentially finite type $A$-algebra $C$, finite $C$-module $P$ and $A$-linear $v:P\to T$ with $T$ flat and $\bar v$ injective: if $P$ is already $A$-flat, then $v$ is universally injective. Use the free-colimit node to write $P=\varinjlim F_d$. Tensor commutes with colimits, so $P/\mathfrak mP=\varinjlim(F_d/\mathfrak mF_d)$. Each map into this last colimit is injective: an element mapping to zero vanishes at a later stage by the elementwise criterion, and the transition map is injective. Thus every $F_d\to T$ is residue-injective. Free modules are projective, so the local projective-source criterion makes every $F_d\to T$ universally injective. For any $A$-module $Q$, write an element of $P\otimes_AQ$ at a stage $F_d\otimes_AQ$. If its image in $T\otimes_AQ$ vanishes, injectivity at that stage kills the representative. This proves the auxiliary implication, with no linearity of $v$ over $C$ needed.

Still with $A$ henselian, prove the assertion when $A\to C$ is essentially of finite presentation and $P$ is finitely presented over $C$; allow the map $v:P\to T$ to be only $A$-linear. Choose the finitely generated ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$ from the quotient-flattening node. It gives $P/IP$ flat over $A/I$. The ring $A/I$ is henselian: a finite $A/I$-algebra is finite over $A$, and the idempotent-lifting criterion for $A$ applies with the same residue quotient. The map $A/I\to C/IC$ is local and essentially of finite type, and $P/IP$ is finite over $C/IC$, as follows by reducing generators and the algebra presentation. Moreover $T/IT$ is flat over $A/I$: tensoring an injection of $A/I$-modules with it is the same as tensoring with $T$ over $A$. The closed-fibre map of $v\bmod I$ is the original injective $\bar v$. Step 1 therefore makes $P/IP\to T/IT$ universally injective over $A/I$.

source.place: Tag 0AT3, second proof paragraph, flattening ideal and reduction modulo I.

proof.text: Tensor $0\to I/I^2\to A/I^2\to A/I\to0$ over $A$ with $P$ and with $T$. Right exactness gives the bottom row $P\otimes_A I/I^2\to P/I^2P\to P/IP\to0$; flatness of $T$ makes the corresponding top row start with zero. In the commutative diagram induced by $v$, the left vertical map is injective: it identifies with $(P/IP)\otimes_{A/I}I/I^2\to(T/IT)\otimes_{A/I}I/I^2$, which is injective by step 2. If an element in the lower left maps to zero in the lower middle, its image upstairs maps to zero, hence is zero by upper-row injectivity, and hence the original element is zero. Thus the lower left multiplication map is injective. Apply the nilpotent-ideal flatness criterion to $R=A/I^2$, its square-zero ideal $I/I^2$ and the module $P/I^2P$. The reduced module is $P/IP$, already flat, so $P/I^2P$ is flat over $A/I^2$.

source.place: Tag 0AT3, displayed diagram and square-zero criterion; the diagram concerns P, not T, in the concluding Tor calculation.

proof.text: By the equivalence defining $I$, now with $J=I^2$, step 3 implies $I\subseteq I^2$. Hence $I=I^2\subseteq\mathfrak m_AI$, so $I=\mathfrak m_AI$. Nakayama for the finite $A$-module $I$ gives $I=0$. The same equivalence with $J=0$ now proves $P$ flat over $A$. Step 1 proves $v$ universally injective. Finite presentation over $C$ was a hypothesis of this case.

source.place: Tag 0AT3, final contradiction, expanded using finite generation and Nakayama.

proof.text: Remove the presentation hypotheses in the henselian case. Choose the local surjection $C=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]_{\mathfrak q}\twoheadrightarrow B$ furnished by the polynomial-cover node and regard $N$ as a finite $C$-module. Put $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal); finite-type Noetherianity and localization Noetherianity show $C/\mathfrak m_AC$ is Noetherian. Write $N=C^s/K$. The image $\bar K$ of $K$ in $(C/\mathfrak m_AC)^s$ is finitely generated by the submodule finiteness node. Lift generators to $k_1,\ldots,k_t\in K$ and put $K'=\sum Ck_j$, $P=C^s/K'$. Then $P$ is finitely presented over $C$, and the surjection $p:P\to N$ is an isomorphism modulo $\mathfrak m_A$, since both residue presentations have relation submodule $\bar K$.

source.place: Tag 0AT2 (lemma-reduce-finite-type-injective-into-flat-mod-m), proof, polynomial cover and finite relations on the closed fibre.

proof.text: Apply steps 2–4 to the $A$-linear composite $P\xrightarrow{p}N\xrightarrow{u}M$. Its residue map is injective by step 5 and the hypothesis, and $A\to C$ is essentially of finite presentation. The composite is universally injective, in particular injective for $Q=A$, so the surjection $p$ is injective and is an isomorphism. Thus $N$ is flat over $A$ and $u$ universally injective. For finite presentation over $B$, tensor the finite presentation $C^t\to C^s\to N\to0$ with $B$. Right exactness gives $B^t\to B^s\to B\otimes_CN\to0$, and $B\otimes_CN\cong N$ via $b\otimes x\mapsto bx$ since $C\to B$ is surjective. This proves all three assertions in the henselian case, even for an $A$-linear map.

source.place: Tags 0AT2 and 0AT3; finite presentation over a quotient obtained directly by base-changing the finite presentation.

proof.text: For general $A$, take the henselization $H$ of the pair $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$. The pair-henselization and comparison nodes give a henselian local ring $H$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_AH$ and residue field $k$. The flat-quotients node says $A\to H$ is flat. Set $D=B\otimes_AH$. The ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_BD+\mathfrak m_HD$ is maximal because $D/\mathfrak n\cong B/\mathfrak m_B$, and put $B'=D_{\mathfrak n}$. The maps $B\to B'$ and $H\to B'$ are local. The latter is essentially of finite type, by extending the finite algebra generators and then localizing. The map $B\to D$ is flat: for a $B$-linear injection, its tensor with $D$ identifies with its tensor over $A$ with $H$. Localization is flat, and composing these tensor injections shows $B\to B'$ flat. It is faithfully flat by the flat local homomorphism node.

Put $N'=N\otimes_BB'$, $M'=M\otimes_BB'$ and $u'=u\otimes_B1$. The chosen generators show $N'$ finite over $B'$. Identify $M'$ with the localization at $\mathfrak n$ of $M\otimes_AH$. The latter is $H$-flat, since its tensor with any injection of $H$-modules identifies with the tensor over $A$ with $M$; localization preserves this flatness. Modulo $\mathfrak m_H$ the ring $B'$ identifies with $B/\mathfrak m_AB$: after quotienting $D$ by $\mathfrak m_H$, its localization is at the maximal ideal of the already local ring $B/\mathfrak m_AB$, hence changes nothing. Accordingly $\bar u'$ identifies with $\bar u$ and is injective. Steps 1–6 applied to $H\to B'$ therefore give $N'$ flat over $H$, finitely presented over $B'$, and $u'$ universally injective over $H$.

source.place: Tag 0AT4, replacement of modules and application of Tag 0AT3; closed-fibre and flatness identifications expanded.

proof.text: Finite presentation of $N$ over $B$ descends from that of $N'$ over $B'$ by the finite-presentation descent node. Also $N'$ is $A$-flat: tensor an $A$-linear injection first with flat $H$ and then with the $H$-flat module $N'$. The faithfully-flat-extension flatness node for $A\to B\to B'$ now gives $N$ flat over $A$. Finally, for any $A$-module $Q$, identify the base change along $B\to B'$ of $u\otimes_A1_Q$ with $u'\otimes_H1_{H\otimes_AQ}$ using associativity, $x\otimes b'\otimes q\mapsto(x\otimes b')\otimes(1\otimes q)$. It is injective by step 8. Faithful flatness reflects exactness of the two-term complex $0\to N\otimes_AQ\to M\otimes_AQ$, so $u\otimes_A1_Q$ is injective. This is the required universal injectivity for every $Q$.
